T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

**Synopsis:**
Gold is steady near $4,469/oz ahead of the US nonfarm payrolls report, with markets pricing roughly a 50/50 chance of a September Fed rate hike. Fed Governor Waller signalled openness to holding rates if inflation continues to moderate, which sparked a 2% gold rally Thursday. The NFP print is the near-term pivot point: a soft number would further reduce hike odds and support gold, while next week's inflation data remains an additional risk factor. Central bank demand is cited as a structural floor. Geopolitical tension (US–Iran, seventh month of conflict) adds background uncertainty. Silver, platinum, and palladium are all tracking modest weekly losses.

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Difference: -35 (More dovish than before) — Fed Governor Waller's signal that he'd support holding rates if inflation moderates, combined with a marginally softer labour market (rising jobless claims), has shifted the near-term narrative meaningfully toward a pause. The 50% hike probability implies the market has pulled back from a more hawkish prior stance, though the outcome remains genuinely data-dependent pending NFP and next week's CPI.
